title: RBAC v2: add permission enum + registry (metadata + CI validation)
author: Jordan Lee
body: Summary: Introduces a canonical permission registry for RBAC v2 in the redwood monorepo. This adds a typed Permission enum (backed by stable string IDs), a registry with required metadata (description, owning team, sensitivity tier, allowed scopes), and CI validation to enforce uniqueness + naming conventions. Motivation: We need a single source of truth for "what permissions exist" before we can (a) annotate endpoints/jobs consistently, (b) generate role templates/policy bundles, and (c) provide audit/evidence artifacts for enterprise customers. This PR intentionally includes only an initial catalog covering the first critical workflows (org/user/role management, API key management, audit log export, routing policy edits) so downstream adoption work can proceed in parallel. Design notes: Permission IDs follow ADR-014 conventions (namespaced dot-separated strings, no implicit wildcards, no environment-specific IDs; scoping is handled in bindings). Metadata is intentionally strict and required for every permission to avoid future "mystery permissions". The registry is compile-time accessible for services and is also exportable as JSON for docs/Console. Implementation details: Added rbac/permissions/Permission.ts (enum), rbac/permissions/registry.ts (PermissionDefinition map), a registry export command (prints machine-readable catalog), and a CI linter step (permissions-lint) that checks: (1) unique IDs, (2) regex match for allowed format, (3) required metadata fields present, (4) no duplicate descriptions with different IDs, (5) deprecated permissions must include replacement + sunset date. Also added unit tests around the linter and registry export. Follow-ups: Endpoint annotations (ENG-18305) will reference Permission enum values directly; Gateway middleware (ENG-18277) will use the registry to populate denial reason context; Docs (redwood-docs PR) will consume the exported catalog. Checklist: [x] Permission ID naming matches ADR-014; [x] Initial inventory reviewed w/ Security Eng; [x] CI enforcement added; [x] Export format documented; [ ] Backfill remaining permissions (tracked in ENG-18241). Risk: Low. This is additive and not yet wired into enforcement paths. CI: New step added to buildkite pipeline; should run <2s.
commits: rbac: add Permission enum + registry definitions
rbac: add permissions linter + unit tests
docs(dev): add README for permission registry + export
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security Eng) — Comment: Love the direction. A couple of asks: (1) Can we require an owning team / oncall field? This is always needed when we get a questionnaire asking "who approves changes to permissions". (2) For "audit.export" can you confirm this covers both Console export and SIEM exporter? I want to avoid split-brain permissions. Also, ensure the naming matches ADR-014 exactly (no underscores).

Jordan Lee — Reply: Added required owner field ("owner_team") to PermissionDefinition and updated lint + existing entries. On audit export: I split into two actions because the data paths differ: "audit.logs.export" (user-initiated export/download) vs "audit.siem.configure" (configure exporter destinations + tokens). Both are in this PR. Also fixed "api_keys.rotate" -> "api_keys.rotate" stays but removed an underscore in one draft entry (now "api_keys.create" etc).

Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authn/Authz) — Comment: Please make sure the enum values are the stable string IDs, not numeric. We’ve been burned by reordering enums. Also would be good to have a function like getPermissionDefinition(id) that throws a typed error if missing, so service middleware can fail closed.

Jordan Lee — Reply: Enum is string-valued. Added getPermissionDefinition() which throws MissingPermissionDefinitionError; callers can treat missing definitions as config error and deny by default. Added tests that the registry covers every enum entry.

Ethan Park (Control Plane) — Comment: For control-plane endpoint annotations we’ll import from this package. Can we keep the API surface dead simple? I’d prefer: Permission.<NAME> and registry lookup internal. Also: please add a short section in README with examples for endpoint annotations + jobs.

Jordan Lee — Reply: Kept exports limited: Permission enum + PermissionId type + getPermissionDefinition + listPermissions. Added README examples for: control-plane endpoint annotation, async job permission mapping, and exporting the catalog for docs/Console.

Amara Diallo (API Gateway) — Comment: The lint rule about deprecation requiring a sunset date is good. Can we also require a replacement permission if deprecated? And can the linter output a clear failure message (actionable) in CI logs?

Jordan Lee — Reply: Updated linter: deprecated requires both replacement_id and sunset_date. CI output now prints a short, greppable line per failure (e.g., PERM_LINT[E003] permission id invalid: ...).
Marcus Lin — Approval: Approved. This is a key building block for the rest of the v2 work. Please ensure follow-up PRs don’t add permissions without sensitivity tiers; CI should catch it now.
release_notes: Internal-only (no customer behavior change): adds canonical permission registry + CI validation to unblock RBAC v2 endpoint annotation and policy bundle generation.
